data.long_meaning: From the Hebrew name Shimon, meaning 'God has heard.' In the New Testament, Simeon is the name of an old man who was told by the Holy Spirit that he would not die until he had seen the Messiah. The name Simeone carries the meaning “God hears” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Simeone usually hope their child will grow to embody god hears and live with faith, good character and purpose.

in_hebrew.name: שמעון
in_hebrew.meaning: הוא שומע אלוהים או שמעון האל
in_hebrew.long_meaning: שמעון הוא שם עברי שפירושו 'הוא שומע אלוהים' או 'אלוהים שמע'. השם שמעון מוזכר בתנ'ך כבנו של יעקב ובתור אחד משנים עשר שבטי ישראל. השם נגזר משורש 'שמע' שפירושו לשמוע, והוא שם נפוץ בקרב יהודים ונוצרים כאחד.

in_greek.name: Σίμων
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Σίμων είναι η ελληνική μορφή του ονόματος העברי שמעון. Στο Ευαγγέλιο, ο Σίμων αναφέρεται ως ένας από τους αποστόλους του Ιησού Χριστού, γνωστός ως Σίμων Πέτρος. Το όνομα σημαίνει 'εκείνος που ακούει τον Θεό' και είναι σημαντικό στη παράδοση της Εκκλησίας.

in_latin.name: Simeon
in_latin.long_meaning: The name Simeon is derived from the Hebrew name שמעון, meaning 'He who hears God'. In the Latin tradition, Simeon is considered a significant figure in the New Testament, often associated with Simeon the Just, who recognized Jesus as the Messiah. The name reflects the spiritual significance of listening to God's will.

in_english.name: Simeone
in_english.meaning: He who hears God or God has heard
in_english.long_meaning: The name Simeone originates from the Hebrew name שמעון (Shimon), meaning 'He who hears God' or 'God has heard'. It is significant in both Jewish and Christian traditions, appearing in the New Testament as Simeon, a devout man who recognized Jesus as the Messiah. The name symbolizes spiritual attentiveness and divine favor.

data.cultural_impact: Simeon is a distinctly Jewish name with roots in ancient Hebrew tradition. It reflects a rich cultural history that celebrates faith and obedience to God's will. In Christianity, Simeon represents the connection between the Old Testament and the New, as he is among the first to recognize and receive Jesus as the long-awaited Messiah.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Simeon is a reminder of God's attentiveness and care for His people. The old man Simeon, who had been waiting for the Messiah all his life, was finally granted the privilege of holding and recognizing the infant Jesus. This story highlights the importance of faith and patience, and the belief that God hears and answers prayer. It is a powerful reminder of the sacred bond between God and His people, and the potential for divinely ordained moments of encounter and transformation in our lives.
